name: Should I build the pool first or the landscape first?

mainEntity.name: Should hardscape, landscaping, and outdoor kitchen work be done before or after custom pool construction?
mainEntity.text: Should hardscape, landscaping, and outdoor kitchen work be done before or after custom pool construction?

acceptedAnswer.text: In most custom outdoor projects, the pool comes before the final landscape finish work. Excavation, steel, plumbing, and shell construction can be disruptive, and heavy equipment can damage completed patios, plantings, and outdoor kitchens. That is why the pool shell and major utilities are usually completed before the final surface materials and planting go in. That said, there are exceptions. Grading, drainage, retaining walls, and underground utility routing may need to happen before the pool is finished. If the project includes an outdoor kitchen, fire feature, or major hardscape layout, the design should be coordinated early so everything aligns with the pool equipment pad, drainage slopes, and traffic paths. The smartest approach is to build the project in a sequence, not as isolated parts. Ask the contractor which items must happen first, which can overlap, and which should wait until after heavy construction ends. This is especially important on smaller Los Angeles lots where access is limited and rework is expensive. A good page on this topic should explain the common order of operations and the risks of installing landscaping too early.
acceptedAnswer.description: The pool is usually built first, then surrounding hardscape and landscaping are completed around it. In some projects, grading, drainage, and utility rough-ins happen first, but finish landscaping usually comes after the pool shell and deck are set. The order matters because access and excavation can damage finished outdoor features.
